Just saying hello to the boys in blue. I'm going to be DA one day and I need to have an open dialogue with the men on the frontline.
I like that.  I just put paperwork away for that bandit from a couple weeks ago that you prosecuted.  He gave us quite a hard time.  I thought he might go free for a while,,,but you got him good.

Ah yes, paperwork. Speaking of, it is a bit cluttered in here, once I'm in office, we'll see about getting someone to clean this place up some. Tedious work. But yes I remember that bandit, bit of a nasty fellow. All of those innocent people and a shame we couldn't catch him quicker.

Yes, we still haven't cleaned up since they ransacked the place for that letter of proof.  That's why I'm taking care of it now and putting things back in order.  One part of the job I don't really like.  Oh, yes...here's the knife that I used to catch the slippery criminal.
*takes knife*
Its bad types like them that made me want to become a sheriff.  What made you want to become a lawyer?

It all started when I learned how to read. I would read stories about good guys and bad guys when I was small. It really hooked me in and I didn't have a choice in the matter. I always won against my opponents in debates and that got me into quite a bit of trouble when i was a boy. Growing up, everything seemed to fall into place and if it didn't I talked my way into place.
That's inspirational!  Hey, I'm going to order some lunch soon. Want to join me?
You trying to bribe me sheriff? haha I would like a bite to eat!
Ha ha, too funny.  Oh great.  While we eat we can discuss that decree from the King about going to speak to children about our jobs...did you get one?
of course, its all about the children isn't it. Who is going to take our place when we are gone?
I wouldn't want the job of filling our shoes.

setting.name: main prayer room
setting.description: This is a room that is large, a prominent place of the temple. Everywhere there are stone benches, and there is colored stained glass on the high walls, a large stone altar is at the head of the room, the walls are adorned with gold and silver ornaments, and the floor is rich with
setting.background: This is a room of worship, the large size and high ceilings amplify the mournful voices of those sacrificing to the gods so that they may be better heard, it is a highly ornamental place to show off the prosperity of the gods

speech: Do you know how to perform your role at tomorrow's service? It's important that nothing goes wrong.
Yes , of course.I work at the church all the time helping the priests
I should have known better than to doubt you. I'm just unusually nervous about this service since the King will be here.
thanks for the vote of confidence.I already cleaned all the stone benches
Thank you. Have you folded the robes and sorted them by size?
Yes.It took me a while, but I did it
Did you complete your studies? I know the headmaster was worried your responsibilities at church were keeping you from your work.
Not all of them.I was very busy getting the prayer room clean and ready
I understand, but your school work is important too. One day I hope that you will be a man of the cloth, like myself. But that will mean you have to do well in school.
I am sorry to disappointed you.Would you want me to resign my post/
No, no. Of course not. Your place is here. Perhaps I can help you study for an hour a day.
Thanks for the vote of confidence.I will try my best
You will be successful. But just in case, let's be sure to pray about it.
That is an excellent idea.Let's pray for success.

setting.name: Apothecary
setting.description: The Apothecary is filled with scores of scores of glass bottles. Each is a different color and has a different concoction. Scales and other types of medical devices line the shelves. There are many beakers and measuring devices. There is an entire walls with bags filled with different colored powders. There is a huge table in the middle.
setting.background: At the Apothecary, medicine is given for everyone, from the townspeople to the king. Villagers can find remedies for all sorts of ailments, from headaches to stomachaches. People come there whenever they have any sort of ailment. They mix the chemicals and powders to create the perfect remedies.

speech: Your majesty! It's an honour to meet you.
You look well. How is your family this day?
They are well. My father has a slight cold which is why I've come to the apothecary. What brings you here my King?
From time to time I like to go to the streets of my people.  I wondered in to this shop and was taken by all of the many different colored bottles.
The colours are truly beautiful. It's really an honour to have you walk amongst us your Majesty. Do you have much knowledge of what the intruments are for?
Hmmm...I wish I could say I do. My magician and healers have such things but not as many as these. Are you a healer yourself or your son perhaps?

Alas no - but I once saw a traveling magician use similar looking things in his performance. My grandmother also practiced a form of alchemy that required a set of scales similar to those on the shelf. Perhaps some of these powders are used for some magical purpose?
I will have the Apothecary send each of the potions to the castle for my healer and magician. Will you join me at the castle three day hence for a meal and some ale?

I would be honoured my King! I wish there was something I could bring as thanks, however I have no food or drink I would dare take to the house of a King. I will also choose some potion for my ailing father - perhaps this red powder? Do you remember what this powder does from what your magician has told you over the years?
I will send my magician to your father at once. Give my guard directions to your home.  My magician will bring the potions that will be needed. Have you a wife?

My eternal thanks your Majesty! My home is at the edge of town, on the road leading to the forest. It is the thatched house next to the water mill. Alas my wife died in child birth. I am left with just a son. Tell me your majesty - will the Queen be joining us for our meal three days from now?
Yes my beautiful queen will be joining us as well as my daughters and their maids.  Please if you can spare him from his chores...bring your son as well.
I will my King! Thank you! He so rarely gets to meet young people his own age! My mates in the inn will never believe I've been invited to dine with the royal family!
I will venture to share with you that I am looking for a new footman. Is your son of sturdy stock?

setting.name: Church Garden
setting.description: The church garden is filled with a variety of useful plants. There are many flowering plants. There is a lot of food grown in the garden. There are carrots, tomatoes, strawberries and a variety of other fruits and vegetables. Fruit-bearing trees provide shade for the garden. The plants are arranged in neat rows. It smells sweet with the flowers. Different colored sticks show the different plants.
setting.background: Many villagers benefit from the produce of the church garden. The fruits and vegetables are used to feed the poor and the hungry. Many people would starve if they did not get the produce from the church garden. They are used for celebrations such as weddings as well. The flowers are used in ceremonies.

speech: Why hello there princess! What brings you to the lovely church garden today?

Oh, hello there... commoner.  Do stand back, I wouldn't want you getting dirt on my gown.  Feel free to admire my glorious beauty from a distance.  I've come for some flowers to set off my golden hair.
O.. of course my princess. I will respect your wishes. Do say, what is the secret to keeping your hair so beautiful? My wife would surely love to know.

I'm afraid it is merely part of my beauty, which makes the poets sing and princes fight in glorious battle over me.  Although my sister does often pilfer my wardrobe in the vain hope that I have some miracle to my beauty.  She certainly needs *quite* a number of servants to even make herself presentable!

Aye, your beauty does certainly seem innate, wonderful quality to highlight indeed. Say, I wanted to let you know about my village. Would you be able to pass some information along to your father, the King?
Hmp.  Well.  It depends, I suppose.  For I am dreadfully busy.

Of course my dear, I'm sure you have many festivities to prepare for. Tis only a small request but we found a delightfully talkative rabbit in our village just this week. As you know we have many magical creatures but a talking rabbit seemed noteworthy enough to alert the royal family about.
Oh my!  That does sound quite fascinating indeed.  What exactly does it speak of?  Is it... is it very pretty?
It's quite plain really but it speaks of battles. A lot of it is far too complex for a simple villager as myself to understand but it seems to be speaking of the future!
Battles, you say?  Are they... battles over a particularly charming and comely princess, perhaps?
You were not mentioned directly my princess. The horrific details that I was able to capture would surely not be anything you would want to be involved in. It all seemed quite dire.

Well, I know that... suffering is... bad.  But if it but of the common people, directed to meet in glorious battle over a winsome princess, then surely tis for a most just cause.  Ah, but think of the ballads that will be composed!

Yes, yes, of course. We do want those bards to keep in good health to write lovely ballads for you though my dear. Please do tell your father of our mystical rabbit and we can bring it to his chambers at once.
Hm.  Well.  I suppose that's true.  I will... consider these words of yours, little man.  Now then, kindly back up three paces so that I may reach those flowers.

setting.name: Dining hall
setting.description: The dining hall is large and airy. Huge candelabras with many candles stand throughout the room. There is one huge wooden table spanning the room that can accommodate a hundred guests. Tapestries with angels line the walls. The chairs are gilded and intricate.
setting.background: The dining room is used for eating for small occasions and large festivities alike. The king and his family always eat here. They have used it for special occasions such as weddings and Christmas dinner but also for family meals. Many important discussions take place over food here.

speech: King. I assume I'm here for an important reason, a hall this large just for me?
You are, indeed. I have brought you here to discuss your possible appointment to my cabinet.
I'm honored. I know the people are calling for it, so for you to listen is very wise. I've never seen grandeur of this nature before
Yes. It seems even the Queen is onboard with the idea. Of course, as a member of my cabinet, you would be traveling quite extensively. How would your family feel about that?

Honestly, that is the part I worry about most. I enjoy spending time with them. Is there any possibility of them travelling with me? I know funds are tight, but for me to fulfill my duties completely, I require the support that having my family at my side gives.
How many children do you have, and what are their ages?
12 at last count. There's no doubt more in the works, sire. To answer your second question: 3 months, 2, 3, 5, 6, 8, 9, 11, 12, 13 and the twins are both 14
Good heavens! That's quite a large family. Perhaps we should try to limit your travel so that you can be home to better support your wife.
Family is important to me, being with them and as you can see, growing it. Perhaps this is a more appropriate arrangement.
I couldn't see you leaving such a brood - or even traveling with them. You would need an entire ship just for your family!
Well then again, with all this ostentation, I'm sure you can personally see to it..
We are fortunate to have you. I assume you can begin work immediately?
You just say the word, sire.
We are having a chamber meeting tomorrow evening. I expect to see you there.

setting.name: The Bottlery
setting.description: The room is dark and the air is still. There are large barrels of wine from various decades. The corners are spotted with cobwebs.
setting.background: The Bottlery is where the kings wines are stored. The wines stored here date back to several centuries.

speech: Princess, you are coming to the age where it's time you be shown The Bottlery.
Is it really necessary? It is really quite grim down here.

It is, indeed. Soon you'll be expected to drink wine at the royal feasts. Last month when your mother served you some you turned your nose up at it. That's not acceptable. In your role, you must learn to at least sip wine.
Mother is gone now, and how I wish I had sipped from her wine. To bring this up at such a time has very much dullen my shine, King.
I realize that. But there is no alternative. And please, call me Father.
You will be my father as long as you stay unmarried to the wretched woman! She truly is a mare, father. I'm shaken to my core by her presence.
You've made your opinion very well known to me and everyone else in the kingdom. I have no intention to marry her. Yet.
Oh whew! Here I was acting proper as a sort of butter up, yikes! Okay crack this wine open, your girl's thirsty!
That's my girl! And apparently you do have a thirst for wine. Please, join me in a bottle- or two!
Get this ghastly thing off for a start. Now which one has the highest percentage. Only the highest percentage for this future queen!
Yes, yes... well, in that case perhaps we should bring out the spirits and the shotglasses.
I'm so happy. For one now that I can relax, and two, how easy it was to convince you not to marry. I thought you were serious with her?
She's problematic to my monarchy. I do care for her, but you hate her and your opinion is not alone. Everyone in the kingdom seems to want her head.
We do not stan the future problematic queen. I'm glad you saw the light!

setting.name: arrow house
setting.description: A small shed with an earthen floor, holds two tables upon which rests neatly arrayed wooden boxes, each of which holds a score of newly made arrows. A third table holds several more large boxes, wherein spent and damaged arrows are placed, so any part still serviceable may be harvested. A few worn practice bows hang upon the walls and a small number tools, as well as replacement strings and polishing equipment rests in boxes under the shelves. Another set of neatly arranged boxes contains newly made parts, for the Fletcher to transform into viable arrows. A small wooden chair completes the furnishings.
setting.background: An old Fletcher carries out his duties, smiling dutifully and politely at the archers and other visitors to his arrow house. He is constantly working, though is known to entertain extended visits from specific masters and the court jester. A master of archery in his own right, it's commonly said that no one in all the land can out shoot him. In spite of challenges, taunts and pleas, he refuses to shoot an arrow, save for when testing bows or new types of arrows.

speech: How goes it, Jester? In need of arrows for some prank?
I guess i came to the right place. Not a prank, more a "display", shall we say.
Hmm? Interesting. Is this just for the king, or will it be public?
It's is for the King, the public will come to realize what has occurred however. I require 99 arrows. I'm not overly worried by the quality, that's not important.
Your words are making me nervous, Jester. These arrows aren't intended to harm the king, are they?
I have 99 absences of arrows. This is my most pressing problem to solve. The problem of the kings welfare I assure you, as they say, "ain't one"
As you say. Are these arrows for the king's army?

Okay I will tell you. The kings daughter is quite fond of my tricks. She has secretly accepted to be part of a display where she is roped to a spinning wheel whilst I fire arrows at her, narrowly missing her legs, arms and royal face. The king has no idea, that's the gag!
Ah, that will be quite the spectacle. You do know the consequences if you happen to miss, right?
If I happen to miss missing Miss? well, Miss will die I suppose or be largely maimed or disfigured. Will the king hate me more than he does? Is that possible?
Well, maybe not, but I highly doubt you'd survive.
And that's where the public come in! Everyone loves a good show. Now.. arrows?
Oh, yeah....sure. Did you say the condition doesn't matter? I can give you these old ones for much cheaper than the new ones.
We'll I guess these damaged arrows on the third table here are cheaper? Any bulk discounts we can add?

setting.name: Castle Kitchens
setting.description: A large room, with pots, pans, serving platters and utensils. Shelves and hooks hanging from the wall hold the implements of the cook's craft. Several wooden counters, as well as a center island are situated around the room. A small table with two chairs is located in one corner. A large fireplace is the central point of focus, with great iron pots resting nearby. The mantel holds several more cooking utensils and the ledge of the fireplace hosts food, currently being warmed.
setting.background: The central location for the life of the serving staff, the Kitchen is bustling with action throughout the day and well into the night. The head cook and his helpers interact with everyone working in the castle and hear all of the gossip, currently making the rounds. Farmers, hunters and others, peddling wares and food find themselves in the always warm confines of the kitchen, often staying for a while to visit and trade the the most recent stories and news.

speech: Who let this child in the Castle Kitchens? We have a large feast to prepare this evening!
I just wanted to see what you're making! Here, wanna try my cookies?
No outside food allowed in the kitchen, we can't have that contaminate the royal feast. Guards! Escort this child out of here.
Wait! What if I do this? *crystal ball drops and evil spirit appears*
Okay kid, I can't deal with your imaginary games right now. We have to get this food ready.
You're no fun! Here, KING, why don't you take this and go hang yourself!
You don't speak to royalty that way!
I don't care about royalty! You're all just a bunch of old mean people! Wait'll my parents hear the way you're treating me!
You're going to get your parents in trouble with the King kid.
My parents ain't afraid of no king! Give me that back, if you're not gonna use it!
Eat this and leave us alone, we have work to do.
Fine! But I'm taking this.
What do you need a sack for?
I don't know! I'm just taking it cuz you made me mad!

setting.name: Bright Path
setting.description: The bright path is lined with roses, lavender, daisies, and lilies. Apple trees sit on a pristinely-manicured lawn. Hedges in geometric shapes sit just beyond the path. The path leads away from the castle and down to a pond full of fish and swans.
setting.background: The bright path provides the perfect respite for guests who want to take a walk and enjoy the fragrant night air after a party. The queen takes this path often with her maids. They walk and gossip about court life.

speech: Oh! Is that a fish?!
Please help..I need to be tossed back into the water. A bird tried to catch me and I wriggled free onto the path.
Oh! Yes yes! I will bring you back. I've never met a talking fish before!
Thank you!  You are most kind.  We try to never talk to humans.  We learn to swim away.
That is so cool! All the chatter in the court has been driving me nuts - humans tend to talk about such unimportant things. What do fish like to talk about?
Not to offend you, but we often talk about how silly human talk is.  So many things don't make sense and everybody thinks something else is important.  We fish always move as one group together
That's what I think, too! Fish seem to have it better! There's such pointless arguing, and everyone is always talking over each other.
I feel sad for you, Your Highness, because I fear you hear even more talking and arguing than usual, being Queen.
Yes, that is very true! It is very tiring. And not to sound spoiled, but I need a new cushion for my throne with how long I have to sit there! So what do fish do for fun?
We like to swim, of course, and jump and blow bubbles.  We also play games...even checkers with the stones in the pond.  You should come down and play wiht me sometime.
Oh! I would love to! It must be so refreshing to get to be in the water all day..although, I guess you don't know much different!  But water is much better than land.

It has its fun moments until the fishermen come our way.  The king used to forbid fishing in the pond but now they come all the time and sometimes we get confused and bite down. I have lost so many loved ones.

Oh, no.... I need to speak to the king about this matter, that is not okay. I am so sorry you've lost so many. We have plenty of vegetables and grains and all other types of food, we don't need to be eating your families!
You are the kindest and wisest queen!  We can do so much for you as well.  We even know where jewels are down in the boggy pond.

setting.name: Dunes
setting.description: A massive hilly landscape that is nothing but sand and a few rocks.  As you walk this area, you can find some human and animal remains along with broken down wood wagons.
setting.background: There is said to be a legendary oasis in the parts with hidden treasure.  Many have come from around the world to attempt to cross the dunes to get there and have failed miserably.

speech: Hello tiny human. You appear to be lost.
I was told that if I go this way I would find my way to the castle where I have been invited.
Well now isn't that grand! Is there a party at the castle? Do you suppose they'd host a dragon?
I hear the King is very kind and his guards are lazy. If I give you my coin would you be willing to give me a ride to the castle?
Ooooh, a coin? What sort of coin?
I will show you but please dragon do not steal it from me.
Now why would I do such a thing? Are you stereotyping, tiny human?
No dear Dragon. Here I will show it to you now. It is shiny and new.  I received it for work I did for the King.
Oh, it glitters so MUCH in the sunlight. What a beautiful treasure you carry.
Do we have a deal Dragon? My coin for a ride to the castle? I will introduce you to the king if you'd like.
Hmmmm. Oh very well. Let me just dispose of the last rider I had and we shall be off.
Oh my...what happened to him...I don't want that to happen to me. Did you fly too close to the sun?
You do realize that I am a flame dragon, yes? Breathing fire, very warm scales, all of that?
Oh, I hope the king is having hot-dogs and marshmallows at his party. You would be a big hit.  My tunic is made from special flame retardant material so I think we can strike a deal.

setting.name: peasant's cottage
setting.description: The peasant's cottage is a fairly simple wood building with a straw thatched roof.  Inside, you have a fireplace and large pot for cooking, a long wooden dinner table, and some hay filled beds lying on the floor.  There are two chests lying inside with personal belongings such as clothes and family heirlooms.
setting.background: The peasants come here to enjoy a meal and rest at the end of a long day.  There are also some celebrations to be had here.

speech: What brings you to  these poor parts, dear spider?
Oh no!  I was hoping you wouldn't see me, but I have gotten bigger this year.  Winter is coming and I am looking for a place to call home and help rid someone's house of insects...might that be you?
Oh, I would love to have a friend such as you
Really?  Not everybody shares your kind sentiments.  I can be quite a help and love to play a good game of marbles as well.
You can play marbles? Where is you family spider, and what is you name? I have never met one as kind as you.
My name is Persivis and my family has moved on to have their own families.  Later in the life of a spider can be lonely.  I have lived years longer than a spider usually does. Do you have any family?
How come you do not have a family of your own? I do not. I live here alone, and I do not have a job. I work just to make ends meet doing the oddest of jobs.
I tell you what...I could spin fine things with my silk and you could sell them for more food.  You have been so kind to allow me to stay that I want to repay you.
Oh, how wonderful! I would love to do so. Is there anything I could provide you with other than a roof to live under?

Any bugs that you don't like...please set them on the windowsill or shew them in my direction...but no, I think that's all I could want.  I can also let you know news far and wide for insects talk a lot even if they don't have brains.
I love a good story! Not much talk goes on out here. The king looks down on us and does not deem us wonder of knowing.
That's shameful. Doesn't he use the wool from all the sheep around here to make his fine garments?
Of course not! He has his own special tailor who raises sheep on their own.
Well, he will be jealous for the silk things we make and soon you will be rich!

setting.name: Royal Bathroom
setting.description: The royal bathroom is a stone room with a long wooden bench and several holes and seats for royalty to take care of business.  There are some tapestries depicting rural landscapes hanging on the walls to give people something to look at.
setting.background: The king often makes a stop here in the morning but he sets out on official business.  Only the royal family can use these bathrooms as everyone else is forbidden.

speech: Father! I've spoken to you about this before. I need my privacy in the bathroom!
Well we only have one royal bathroom! Where else shall I go to empty my royal bladder?
You could at least wait! A lady needs her privacy, especially in the privy! And besides, you leave a malodorous reign in your wake.
How dare you insult the royal bowels of the kingdom! You know I am a fearless king! I don't hesitate to charge into battle. Especially when nature calls...
Clearly, Father! And normally, I'm happy to have you with me all the time. But ladies have special needs.
But I really can't hold it....it's an emergency...
Oh, fine... I'll wait here while you go, but make it snappy. I really hope it's just pee.
Thank you! Now hold this while I go relieve myself..
Seriously? I'm not holding your scepter while you take a royal dump.
I promise it's not. It would be unfitting for the king to relieve himself on the sidewalk!
Yes yes, I understand. Just please hurry hurry. My bladder is about ready to burst, too.
See! I was done before you could even blink! Now carry on with your business here..
Thank you. But please, leave me alone to my business.
Certainly! I have royal affairs to attend to. You have this entire place to yourself now. Carry on..

setting.name: Back of the stall
setting.description: The back of the store is stocked with everything you can imagine, spices, herbs, jars, vials, bags, colors everywhere. Along with a small bed in the corner of the room for the shopkeeper to sleep in. Next to that there's a small bed for a cat. The bed's are lined with bright red sheets. To the left of the bed there is a small wooden desk with a stool tucked under it. There's a small window to the right of the bed that lets in sunlight which is bouncing off the red blanket thus making the room glow red. It feels comfortably warm.
setting.background: The back room was first made when the shopkeeper realized there were many night where he'd fall asleep at his desk. He his wife fashioned him a small bed that they both transported over by their only horse. On occassion their horse would peer into the back room window and watch over his owner while he slept. Then every morning they'd both head back home to get ready for the afternoon workload.

speech: hello, cat
Hello horse. How's the weather out there today?
It's beautiful. How is the mouse hunting going?
With all of the travelers moving in and out of this shop, it's keeping me busy enough. If it stays nice enough I might have a little nap over on that sunny spot.
I think that's a wonderful idea. Maybe the king will come to the stables today to ride.
Oh, pardon me, I didn't realize I was speaking to the royal horse your grace.
Why thank you. In that case, I shall declare you a royal cat
As it has been decreed, so it shall be. Time for a royal snack.
That's kind of gross. Would you like to share some of my hay? Be careful not to eat the queen's favorite bird! It's the yello finch.
Dang. I was saving that one for later. I guess I'll just give it back.
Thank you. Where will your travels take you today?
Possibly to the back of the shop, maybe over to that ledge by the window. I don't go many places while I have such a cushy life.
There is a nice spot over near the window that has lots of sunlight.
That's the one I was going to take a cat nap in later while you're on your ride with the king.

setting.name: Prisoners Cells
setting.description: The dungeon is filled with the same light of the enchanted torches. Cells line both walls and extend for what feels like miles. There are crates between each cell that store food and a change of clothes for the prisoners. You can hear trickles of water dropping in from the ceiling. It can be deafening at times.
setting.background: The prison was created to hold the mightiest of enemies. The wizards who built it warded it as heavily as they could. Some even lost their lives by using too much magic then they could handle. They say at times you can still hear them chanting, keeping a watch over the prisoners.

speech: Visit is over, it's time for you to go.
Please wait, let us visit a little longer
No. Time up or I can arrange another prisoner's stay down the hall.
No! Not that! Can you at least get me some food?
Maybe after visitor is gone I will see what I can do
Can you at least pass me a change of clothes for now. Its damp down here and I have been wearing this for days.
Yes. let me see if there are any more dry ones here
Give me the keys!
No! now I get to report your failed attemp to escape to the king and watch as your executed
I am innocent! I need to get back to my family!
Too bad..... you trying to escape doesn't prove your innocent only shows you can't follow your king's laws and ends your chance at freedom ever again
The King was going to have me hanged either way. Let me out, I will take my family and leave.

Even if you could get passed me you would not make it to your family, you couln't even make it to the entrance seeing as its guarded at all times too. Then you could watch as they all pay for your crimes
I will strangle you and every guard in my path. I will have my freedom!!!

setting.name: Countryside
setting.description: The countryside is quite nice, it's not filled with a lot of people but with travelers here and there. Some in small groups some on their own. They are hosting a campfire where everyone has some to sit and is telling stories about their adventures. Someone is showing local children how to wield some weapons. Another is offering lodge, and stable for travelers and their animals.
setting.background: The countryside outside the bazaar has always been well known for being a place for people to relax. As they travel back and forth they can stop by campfires and share stories. It was first started by their king. A lovely man who wanted everyone to try and get to know each other and help each other. When he died his villagers wanted to continue his acts of kindness by offering help to those who passed by.

speech: Why aren't you over with the other children learning how to wield some weapons, child?
I saw something shiny over here in the field, and came to see what it was. Look!

OH MY! Look what we have here. I believe this used to belong to the wicked witch of the west who used to lurk this countryside with terror. They say if you talk to the ball then she will reappear. This...This is dangerous, my child!
Really? Oh no! I didn't mean to talk to the witch!!
Have you already talked to it and provoked it?!
....not on purpose! I promise I didn't mean to!
What did you say?!
I told the crystal it looked pretty, and that I would try and find it's owner.
Did the ball respond? TELL ME, what did it do?
I...I...don't think it did anything! Is it doing anything now?
It is spinning. Say, is it locating the witch....did she locate herself... oh no, this is terror on the town
I'm sorry! Oh no! What should we do?

We will give it to the miner, and he will throw it into the hole and deep cave they are mining from. For there the witch will inhabit if she is to come back, or maybe the hole will be too deep for her to ever find her way.
Oh, I hope that will work! You don't think the witch could fly out of the cave do you??
action: give a crystal ball to king
give a crystal ball to miner

setting.name: Saokra's Blacksmith Shop
setting.description: Saokra's Blacksmith Shop is lined with weapons. They are shown through the outside windows, and once you step inside you see everything from bo staffs to canons. Most of the shop is cool for the work that goes on inside. There are dozens of painted maps on the walls and ceiling. There's a bookshelf over to the left side of the shop that holds nothing but rolled up scrolls, and some have fallen to the floor. Armor sets adorn the manikins to the back of the room. There's a vibrant royal blue knight set of armor that causes the back area to light up in a cool glow of blue. The middle of the room has sunlight beaming into it via a skylight that gives the area a warm feeling.
setting.background: Saokra's Shop has been around for years, Saokra herself has always been the owner of it. No one's sure how but it's believed that she was once a God, and possibly still is but instead of living her life in the heavens she chose to live with the people and enjoys her work. One of the reasons for this is that the shop in question seemed to be around for more than a hundred years and with each weapon or armor set she creates you can feel a hum within it. No one's sure why she decided to live the life she does but everyone is grateful to her for having helped keep some of the bad souls away.

speech: Brave knight I bet this is your favorite store in the knigfom
Absolutely! There's nothing I love more than battle. So being around all this really gets the blood going!
Meet my son here he hopes to one day be like you
Oh well hello there young lad! You can definitely be like me. Always be courageous and willing to serve a purpose greater than yourself!
Those are very inspiring words you better take this to heart son if you ever hope to be like this warrior
Indeed, it's a long tough road being a knight. You have to be strong and fearsome. It's not easy in the royal army..
But our king deserves only the best knights possible and it seems you are
Oh don't make my head grow from so many compliments. I still need to fit into my helmet for battle!
Ha humorous too we are the muggiest kingdom and it makes sense
You know, most people in this town avoid me because they think I'm stubborn and argumentative. But you and your son are on my good side...
I never like to assume about anyone I’m just a nice family man
Well that's great! You definitely earned my respect and a tab that you can use in my shop
I will return as soon as possible and get my son his first weapon to begin training you are very honorable
Great news! I'll even give him his first lesson!

setting.name: main foyer
setting.description: The main foyer is massive. A grand staircase sits to the back of the foyer leading to the upstairs. At the front of the foyer stand two servants ready to help anyone who comes to visit. To the left of the room there is a doorway leading into a corridor. To the right there is a door leading to another corridor for the King's servants. At the foot of the stairs there is a bearskin rug that is staring at you almost as if still hungry. The walls are lined with portraits of the king and his family.
setting.background: The foyer is actually the biggest single room in the castle, the King instructed to make it as big as possible so that it could accommodate any family, royal or otherwise that might visit. He wanted every painting of their family they had to be displayed on the walls, so that you could see how long his linage extended.

speech: Good morning, servant. What visitors do I have this morning?
None so far, my lord. However, your daughter was looking for you.
What did she need from me? I hope it's not about that pauper suitor again.
I couldn't quite understand her, as she was talking so extremely fast, but it was something about a boy and a "date".
She does talk rapidly, doesn't she. Did she say if she would leave that castle walls?
Yes, it seems she will be travelling by horseback to the nearest kingdom tonight.
Did she take her compliment of guards at least? Or do I have to send out search parties like last time?
I think it will be fine this time, my lord. She was accompanied by four royal guards when she was getting prepared.

Well at least she sees reason sometimes. And my guards should make sure she doesn't wander off. Please send in my cupbearer. I could use a spot of wine after thinking of my daughter's marriage prospects.
Yes, right away my lord.
Excellent. A dark red should suffice. Has anyone else come to court today?
No, another quiet Saturday as usual, I suppose. Things aren't as busy as they used to be.
It seems that way, what with the dragon finally being slain.
And thank god for that, houses seemed to be burning down every day!

setting.name: hidden revolutionaries' headquarters
setting.description: Inside the revolutionaries' headquarters, you will find a map of the castle and the surrounding town.  Also, you will find a long list of grievances against the King, both by his subjects and the Queen herself.  In addition, there are crates full of weapons and armor, as well as a small vial of poison.
setting.background: This room is used by the Queen and her lover, the Duke of Nottingham, to plot the downfall of the King  They plan to poison the King, who is an evil tyrant, and use the arms and armor to round up and dispatch, if necessary, the members of his inner circle.  Then they plan to announce the Queen as the ruler and the Duke as the long lost King's brother who had been targeted for assassination by the King.  However, the Duke survived, but the King married his grieving fiance.

speech: Oh! this throne is killing me!
It won't just be the throne, ma'am, if these grievances hold any substance. I'm worried for your safety.
I had enough of this books! I need to get some fresh air and see the sun!
The words within these books may be our only saving grace, ma'am. Perhaps if words are not your weapon, we arm ourselves more obviously? There is an army's worth of armor and swords in here.
Duke, teach me how to use this sword...
You're the head of the revolutionaries, ma'am. There's no need for modesty, your skills are renowned. Where on this map will our first assault take place?
I think we need to use this poison. It is the easiest way although not the one that I want to do. The king trusts you like his own. Will you take the risk?

If the poison is detected, there is going to be an uprising. The whole headquarters will be exposed. They have found a very unique way of detecting poisons in their food. They use dogs, ma'am. Very radical but they have been very effective and a set back for us. Perhaps there is something within this pouch?
This... this is a very rare herb, duke... I think if we make a poison from this her, this could be our answer!
Perhaps the dogs won't have encountered this! It still comes with a risk though. Can we be this impulsive? Perhaps some ball play whilst we ponder on the matter?

I'll put it in this pouch and please bring to the alchemist. Tell him this is from me and he will know what to do. I will prepare some men outside the castle to prepare for attack. We'll put this poison in their food and weakened the army as well
As you wish, ma'am.
Duke, be careful! I want you to come back to me safely!

setting.name: Knife Seller
setting.description: The wooden shop's walls are adorned with a variety of steel, iron, and bronze knives. They vary in shape and size, with some being curved and others being small enough to conceal.
setting.background: The Knife Seller has operated as a family business for nearly a decade, in collaboration with a family of blacksmiths who supply the knife sellers with their merchandise. It is a popular seller for the soldiers of the town.

speech: This will be very useful in close battle.
What battle art thou preparing for, soldier?
Battle against the squabbles down south trying to invade the Kings territory.
Aye, good to know ye are loyal to my King.
Of course art thou also preparing for battle?
I look over the shops wares as I talk with you....I am always at battle against anyone that would harm my liege, and I try to always be prepared.  *I hold up my mace*
Ah!!! But you must always guard your weapon!! I’ve shown you no ill will!
You don't want to EVER touch a knight's weapons, boy, I whisper in a menacing tone as the three spears I've stolen from you wind up with their points pressing into your tender throat flesh.

agents: horse tied up in front of a shop

setting.name: Horse Tent
setting.description: Held erect by large bronze poles planted firmly in the ground, the purple and gold Horse tent offers a canvas over a number of stalls, each with it's own accommodations including fresh hay and a trough that is refilled daily. The tent's entrance is kept open during the day to allow sunlight to shine into the tent illuminating those inside, while the other end of the tent has a door leading directly into the guest castle.
setting.background: The Horse Tent is used to store the royalty's guests' horses as they visit the kingdom. They are tended to by the stable boys, and are a means to show the King's generosity in dealing with visitors.

character: a horse tied up in front of a shop
a horse tied up in front of a shop

speech: Please, untie me.I deserve to be free.
Why would i want to do that?
Because you are a kind human being.
well, i am a kind human being of a truth, but the king would have my head on a stake if i let one of his favourite horses go
If you free me, I could be your horse and wokr for you
And could be dead too
Wake up and be a men for the first time in your life.
I would be more of a dead man if i let you loose
You are a waste of time. What are you even doing in this tent??
Taking a wonderful nap, till you spoilt it with your silly request
This is a horse tent, not a hotel for you to take a nap.Don't you have a job?
I take my naps anywhere i feel like
the only reason the tent is open during the day is to allow sunlight to shine, not to let vagabonds like you to enter
Vagabond!!! that's pretty funny

setting.name: Gold Room
setting.description: A hidden room, the Gold Room is adorned with gold candle fixtures on either side, and a gold plated wooden table in the center. Riches lay all around the room and on top of the table. Here can be found the crowns of past kings and the royalty of conquered nations.
setting.background: The Gold Room is where the current Monarchs store their prizes from conquest and their most prized possessions. The location is forbidden by the general public, and hidden to all but the Monarchy's most trusted servants.

speech: *starts to dust crowns* I must get this place cleaner than it has ever been!
Be quick about your work, servant. The King is uneasy when servants enter the Gold Room.
I am only here to please the king. I would never steal from him.
So says everyone. Yet always someone tries.
Have, um you, every... tried?
Watch what you say! If what you said was heard, it's off to the gallows for you and the front lines for me. .
*hold arm in pain* I am sorry to disobey you, I meant no harm by my words. It's just, I haven't been able to go see my family in some time. You know, a little coin would help that.
Hm. Well, on that we might agree. But you're better off sneaking out to cover shifts at the tavern. The punishment will be less severe if you're caught.
The king never give me a day off. Ever! He is so cruel to the lower class.
Your insubordination knows no bounds! I shall report this to head servant. You'll be lucky to avoid the dungeons.
I'm sure the dungeons could not be worse than what I am already forced to do!
Don't get any ideas. And you are wrong. Very wrong. The stories from the dungeon guard keep me up at night. If you want better conditions I suggest you work harder.
I spend my days working hard, just look around! The castle is immaculate, all because of me! And I get nothing! But being torn away from my family.
I've had enough of you. Finish your job and go away.

setting.name: The throne room
setting.description: The throne room features a large Bronze throne surrounded by Iron statue of guardsmen. These guardsmen are crafted to each bare a unique appearance. Below the king's throne there is a silk red carpet pathway that leads to the front gate. The front gate is protected by two armed men who cross swords at the foot of the gate.
setting.background: This provides the main area for the King to meet with diplomats and serve orders to his army. It is not to be accessed by the towns folk and only those close to the king are allowed entry into this heavily guarded area.

speech: Don't you worry folks. I am here to protect you
And how do you think you will do that? We have months of pay we are yet to receive!
That is not my problem.I am here to defend the city
It becomes your problem when we are out of food sir!
I am trained to be in the king's special army.I am an elite soldier
I'll make this an army of farmers. Your days of battle are over.
Are you dumb or something.You just said the town is broke!!
I said I'm broke sir. From poor sales of my crops! I will hit every one of you, one by one. Just a moment.
We are and elite of soldier trained intensely.You got no chance against us
Perhaps we have a common enemy? The king?

setting.name: Throne room
setting.description: The throne room is a lavishly adorned stone fortification, with large purple and gold tapestries hanging on the walls. Between each tapestry there is a painting of the previous ruling families' patriarchs. At the center of the back wall sit's a large throne adorned with gold and silver, with a red silk cushion on it's seat.
setting.background: The throne room is where the king of the castle meets with other diplomats and rules over his kingdom. Only those close to and trusted by the King are allowed into this room, and it is heavily defended by the knights of the castle.

speech: Greetings Your Majesty. I have come as you requested. What matters do you wish to discuss wuith me?

It's rather trivial actually. Seen that tapestry? Third one in. Have it removed, It feels like the eyes are following me around. I have enough of that from the public to have to worry about it in my throne room.
Yoiur majesty, I am a diplomat and a noble, don't you have servants to do such tasks?
Are you not one of them? Regardless, do you not agree? Start here and walk down to the table by the door, and keep watch on the eyes.
I agree about the tapestry and I do as my king orders me to do. I shall take it away. Is there anything else sire?
Oh there were diplomatic matter obviously! You are the diplomat, no? The kitchen need blue cheese, and our ties with France are, shall we say, weathered. Do something about it please.
Blue cheese?! You really are a simpleton, aren't you.? I think I shall do my duty and kill you!
Attack me? At least come armed weakling, here try this.
Your son the Prince is right, you are insane!
I haven't heard that name in years. Ever since that ghastly hat he returned in after his little excursion to the second hand store. I had him exiled.
Exiled? He's the crown Prince. Why would you exile him? Am I to be executed now for attacking you?
Nah, you're cool. I like a worthy adversary. Oh merchant, I had overlooked your presence.
I think I must be dreaming. If you are finished with me sire, I shall go and see about your blue cheese.
Take the merchant with you, his presence has actually made me feel a little off, I regret the hug after all.

setting.name: town center
setting.description: The town is small, but its streets are full of personality. Each building that lines the cobblestone is a different hue, from the purest cerulean to the darkest mauve. Town favorites include a candy shop, brimming with personality - you can taste the candy floss on your tongue as you walk past. You might also enjoy the general store - you can find anything and everything you might need there, including what you did not know you needed. Chairs line the streets for visitors to sit and chat with friends they might find while out exploring.
setting.background: The small, quaint town was born of a necessity for lightness and levity during the dark times. Though the rest of the surrounding world might be brimming with turmoil, here in this tiny hamlet there is merriment and light oozing from each crack in the sidewalk.

speech: Why hello there, welcome to the town. I don't think I've seen you here before.
Hello Horse. You are correct, my family and I are brand new to this land.
Well, welcome! Be sure to introduce yourself to the king. Usually you can find him on my back, but thankfully he's giving me a bit of a break right now.
Say, you wouldn't happen to be knowledgeable about the tax rates in this Kingdom? My family is thinking of settling here.
That's definitely something I don't know anything about, but that salesman over there might be able to help you with matters of gold.
Just one other quick question. Can all of the horses talk here? I've never really met a talking horse before.
Yes, in fact. One of the king's court wizards has a bit of a sense of humor, and took the time to put a spell on each horse in the town giving us the ability to speak.
Now, I have a few horses of my own. Will I be able to get the spell for them? Or would you recommend that I keep them nonspeaking.
Well, I may be a bit biased, but I think we horses have a lot of good advice that would be very helpful, especially to a newcomer.
You've been so helpful. I truly appreciate it. Is there anything that I can do to repay your help?
Well, now that you mention it, I am feeling rather famished. I don't suppose you happen to have a carrot you'd be willing to part with?
I'd love to give you a treat, but for some reason I am unable to do so. Would you settle for this stick?
Hm, a bit less delicious, but I suppose it'll do. Thank you, traveler.
I need to buy a few things, can you tell me if this salesman is trustworthy? I'

setting.name: castle kitchen
setting.description: This is a warm, luxuriant-smelling kitchen, made of red brick that is cool to the touch on the perimeter. In the center of the room stands a grand fire-burning stove, which is stoked with crackling logs and white-hot flames. The perimeter of the room is lined with stone shelves, filled to bursting with pots and pans and other kitchen implements, the light of the fire shining in their reflection.
setting.background: This kitchen is staffed by professional chefs and the most smug wait staff possible. Throughout the day you can see the snooty servants walking back and forth, carrying everything from fresh crusty loaves of bread to elaborate dessert puddings. The kitchen is never empty, for either the King or the Queen is always hungry at some point throughout the day.

speech: Got any goodies today, Chef?
Today's menu is... ratatouille, believe it or not. How does that sound?
Sounds like you're cooking my family up...
How could I deny the king fresh meat when it wanders so willingly into our midst?
You think that is funny? It is not. For we give you diseases
Wow, where were you hiding this?
I carry it with me at all times for protection.
Okay, I apologize. We
What is this paper here?!
It's obviously the recipe. Can I have that back please, it isn't as simple as it looks
Say, can I have some seeds and grain? So I do not have to ruin the people's food...
That seems very basic. this kitchen is the perfect place to make bread. Perhaps you could have that? Just keep your profile low and don't let yourself be seen.
What is the catch here? You people are not usually nice to us mice.
You seemed to like the recipe, would you like to help me with the royal cooking?

setting.name: The Grand Desert
setting.description: The Grand Desert seems to go for miles. The sand is golden and the sun glistens over the endless mounds. There are tents of all different colors scattered throughout the Grand Desert. Magenta and gold, blue and green, all different color combinations of triangular tents outline the sand mounds. Camels and palm trees are seen in the vast distance. The sky looks extraordinarily blue against the tents and sand. No clouds are in sight.
setting.background: The Grand Desert is the King's getaway from royal life. He goes there every year for a break from the kingdom. Here he will be greeted by dancing girls, delicious Arabian meals, and relax far from the stresses. At night he will sit by the fire and listen to the music while others dance in delight.

speech: I am a camel of the knight's desert
Do you mind if I use you for shade? It is so hot out here.
Nae bother people do it all the time!
Perfect. So what brings you out here all alone?
I have been trained to travel point to point to deliver goods. In this case, a jewel
A single jewel? It must be pretty damned important!
That's right. I have traveled in the king's caravan!
Ahh so a jewel for the king, that makes a lot of sense.
Well it is  for  someone in his court. They don't give me details!
Well that is quite exciting, how far off are you?
A VAST DISTANCE UNFORTUNATELY!
Is that so? How far do you figure?
100 miles.
Wow that outta take quite a while! I'll need to climb onto you for a ride if that's the case, we're headed the same way.

setting.name: Hidden garden
setting.description: There are plenty of roses, wilted, but still red.  A large statue of a beautiful woman stands in the middle, ivy growing around her.  She seems very kind in her expression.  It seems as though she may be buried underneath.  There is an overgrown mess of plants that form an archway that she is staring at.
setting.background: This is where the King buried the love of his life who died in childbirth.  She was very fond of dancing.  The king has not visited in some time and it is forbidden for others.

speech: Would you help sir?
Certainly, Madame. How can I assist you?
I see ivy growing in your garden, I may been to free yourself of some. Do you have a penchant for concoctions?
Of what manner of concoctions do you speak? Edible concoctions? Or concoctions that cause enchantments?
I have done wrong. My son is a monster who killed all his brother's in law. I couldn't stand for it but my outspeaking over the situation has landed me in jail. You see, my son is... the king.
Good heavens! So you came to the garden to escape or to fetch items for a spell?
A poison in fact. Thats why  have my eye on that ivy.
A poison to do in the King? I'm not sure I want to be involved with this. I have known of his evil ways for many years, but I am frightened.
Everything I have done thus far in life I regret. Spare this one grace for a woman baring too many mistakes to make a full recovery, yet enough power to make a final jab at redemption.
And if you do take the King's life, who will that leave in power?
I hadn't thought that far ahead. Your'e very wise. I suppose one of my embittered daughters would find her way up

Hmm... perhaps there is another way to take your wrath out on the King. He is evil, but he rules our nation well. Perhaps a poison that disables him but keeps him alive and thus does not strip his reign?
You speak as if from experience. Do you have a plant in mind that could aid in such a task?
A good dose of this hemlock would cause paralysis but not death, assuming he doesn't have too much.

setting.name: Lavoratory
setting.description: The lavatory contains a long trough for which the knights can use for urination. Crude toilets are also included for defecation. The design is all stone walls with candles, and no privacy walls.
setting.background: The room is not very pleasant since there is no ventilation to the outside. The smell can become rancid, but this is somewhat curbed by the cleaning performed by the servants. Servants will come and scoop out the troughs and toilets into wheelbarrows three times per day and wheel the waste to a nearby creek. Once a night, they will scrub the insides, as well, to help get rid of leftover waste.

speech: How do you do today, your majesty?
Very well. Tell me, what is your duties here.
Just cleaning the lavoratory as I am told, then doing the rest of my chores.
I see. My knights are a reflection of me, I expect their quarters, even the lavoratory, to be spotless. Understand?
Of course, your majesty. I have served you for long enough to know that!
Wonderful. There is a lot to be done and I know a fine subject like yourself will see it happen.
I swear to you that I will work diligently!
Are the knight's suits ready and their horses tended to?
Yes, sir! All shined and oiled, and the horses fed and ready!
And tonight's feast needs to be perfect. The queen has been under the weather and could use a good meal.
Of course, I'll make a hearty warm meal for her to feel better. Perhaps a beef stew with red wine?
Excellent. I have big plans for tomorrow, and I will make our neighbors respect my god given authority...Hmm, I am not sure why I concern you with these things.
Hmm well I'm glad you trust me with such vital information.
Don't let my friendly slips of the tongue make you forget your place. I believe you are falling behind schedule.

setting.name: Tub
setting.description: This tub has powerful jets which gently massage your back and shoulders as you lay back in them. It's deep enough to cover your entire body with water, but no too deep that you feel like you are swimming. There is also a handy shelf upon which to place a book or drink.
setting.background: The tub is a magical place that instantly whisks away any negaitve thoughts you had before climbing into it. The king uses it to feel refreshed and energized after difficult days dealing with the problems of his subjects and staff. It is a hidden secret reserved only for the King.

speech: What a miserable existence we live serving the king all day.
Is there anything I can do to make it easier for you?
No you work hard enough for the king.
Thank you. I try. Well, soaking in water is a nice way to get away, at least.
Yes these tubs are truly magical.
Yes they are. Life's not so bad. It's hard sure, but now and again we get moments like this.
I just wish I was born to a different family then I'd be the rich one.
True enough. But hey, at least you have the option to marry rich. I'll be busting my back my whole life.
As a simple subject I do not think so.
Well, you can improve your circumstances to some degree via marriage, anyway. Or perhaps you could work up the ranks in the military. Again, not an option for me.
Indeed but we must work so hard to accomplish so little.
That's true. And whenever we invent clever ways to save work, they find more work for us to do!
Yes its truly quite the short straw to have drawn
Well, at least we have the tub.

setting.name: Along the Pews
setting.description: The alter faces west so the rising sun hits the cross just right each morning. The bejeweled cloth that lay over the alter sparkle and the room practically glows.
setting.background: People come far and wide to this church as it produces an almost magical atmosphere. People claim miracles have happened here because it is so beautiful.

speech: Please, sir- I only have this moldy bread to eat and I'm starving to death. Is there any food here along the pews?
Hm tastes fine to me. Why, I am sure I have some spare food back at the Palace. You should come by tomorrow morning.
Hey! That's my bread - it's my only food! I can't believe you ate the only bits of food I have.
Take this, peasant. It will buy you three days worth of bread. Its not much but its all I can give .
Thank you, thank you! I have a small child and we have been suffering. I am a hard worker- is there anything I can do to repay your kindness?
Wash this towel for me and bring it back tomorrow.
I will be happy to do that for you. Please let me know if there is any work I can do for you or around the church. I'll do anything for food.
Come by to the palace tomorrow and I can speak to you about becoming a gardener. Have you any gardening skills?
Thank you, sir! My aunt was a gardener for the King and I used to go to work with her and help her. I wouldn't say I'm an expert gardener, but I will do a great job.
Ahh, you must shower and wear clean clothes if you decide to visit me.
Yes, it's true, I am rather smelly. I'll be certain to bathe and put on clothes without stains.
Whats in this, Peasant?! Jewelry? Where on earth did you find this?
Hey! I found these outside the church. Finders keepers! I stole nothing!
Forget it! I knew there was something funny about you. You're a petty thief!

setting.name: Courtyard exterior
setting.description: Paths as well as vines, fountains, and sitting areas are decoratively placed through out the courtyard. It's a place where people are welcome and arrive to enter the castle of the court.
setting.background: Centuries old but maintained to look as good as it ever has. It's suppose to be a place to make the people of the kingdom feel like their king is a servant to them not them being servants to a king. People gather and arrive here to see the king, petition the court or just meet with friends who live or work at the castle.

speech: How do you do old friend!
As usual, just trying to find the best deal posible.What about you?
Doing my work as a mule, same old terrible life but that is why I drink!
Just hang in there, my friend.Things will be better
Thank you, but I must get back to work soon.
Take this, my friend.This bag could be of use for you
You do so much for me friend.
Look at this path of vines and fountains.Is in it beautiful?
Yes I love coming here when I have free time...
I love to travel to all places to see things like this place.
Yes its truly a wonder what mankind can do when given the tools.
this rope I bought in china.It is of a best quality.
Ah I see, are you here to sell it to the king?
I wish, but I am not royalty.I do not have the connections to meet the king

agents: there is also a young woman selling flowers to passersby

setting.name: the kitchens
setting.description: The kitchens are a busy, hot place. They are filled with kitchen staff rushing around to prepare the main meals for the king's family and residing nobles. Tonight they are preparing two deer the king and his nobles caught while hunting, as well as some rabbit from a few days ago and seasoned vegetables. There are multiple fires around the kitchen to cook the animals and boil the vegetables, and combined with the heat of all the people the room is stifling. While the main kitchen workers are middle aged women who stay at one station, there are also younger children running around taking ingredients from one place to another. People are shouting instructions and gossip to one another constantly, so it is very hard to hear anything, but the atmosphere is very cheerful.
setting.background: This room has always been the kitchen for the king's family. The kitchen workers take pride in serving delicious food to the king, his family, and whatever guests they may have. In fact, when there are guests, the workers make sure the food is especially delicious. They also have an ulterior motive to make sure the food is amazing - they are allowed the eat the leftovers after the evening's feast is finished.

speech: My I love the smell of fresh food. I wonder whats on the menu today.
Your Majesty I have flowers for your tables tonight.
Wonderful. And here are the books on Marxism that you were so curious to read
Thank you your Majesty.  There are cart loads of flowers in the back. May I borrow a couple of the children to help me bring them in to your tables?
Of course. Make sure to wipe down your feet before you enter the main halls.
Yes Ma'am I will make sure everyone feet are clean before entering the halls.  Everything smells so wonderful.
Which flowers did you bring me today? I hope you got fresh roses, surely.
Yes your Majesty they are your favorite. But if I may be so bold as to say none as lovely as you.
Why thank you. But I'm afraid I can only envy your own youthfulness and luscious hair.
Thank you ma'am you are too kind.  Our king sent a piece of material that matched your dress for tonight and we were able to get flowers to compliment it.  I pray you will approve.
How lovely and what a nice surprise. Why don't you also attend tonights ball?
Oh...your Majesty...I am but a shop girl...I would not have anything appropriate to wear for such a beautiful ball
I have some old dresses that might fit you. Its the Queen's order that you attend!
Your Majesty honors me. I will accept your invitation of course but first I must get the flowers inside to the tables. May I take my leave your majesty?

setting.name: Blacksmith
setting.description: The sounds of metal and steel clanking together can be heard as you approach the Blacksmith. Varieties of shiny maces, swords, and spears are stung on shelves that line the walls in the shop. A big, burly man can be seen hammering away at swords as he brazens them through the melting pot. His young apprentice greets the customers. The walls are blackened from soot by the fire pit.
setting.background: Funded by the King himself, this was once the armory for the Kings Guard but as the Kingdom expanded, the Blacksmith was turned into one open to the citizens of the kingdom. The Blacksmith shop was destroyed in a fire during the second medieval war but was reconstructed on request of the king to where it stand now in the center of the Bazaar.

speech: I heard your scepter was in need of some work. Perhaps I can fix it at my blacksmith shop.
That's right. Well done. I also want to know about the latest sword technology.

First let's address your scepter. It seems like two of the rubies have become loose. I can tighten this up by applying some heat to the gold. If you don't mind leaving it with me, I can fix it overnight.
I am pleased. Any idea on the cost?
Sire, I work for the kingdom. All of your work is already included in my pay. I am completely at your service.
And this is why I also wanted to come here: we want to adorn your sign with the royal coat of arms to show you are an approved supplier to the King's Armory.

Oh, that would be perfection itself! Now, let me tell you about the new sword technology. We have begun to make a sword with a blade that extends much further down. This ensures greater penetration through both muscle and bone.
very interesting. Are production times similar?
Only slightly longer, and the cost of materials is the same.
I see. But you think the improvements in performance are worth it?
Definitely, Sire. Our current swords get nicked by the bones, and their performance decreases greatly after a couple of kills. These would hold up much better.
So the longevity factor is worth considering too?
Of course, of course. And with the state of politics, longstanding wars might be coming. We simply must be prepared. I won't be able to keep up with the repairs otherwise.
Yes, our kingdom is one of peace and will keep out of any conflicts unless they relate to self-defence; but be assured that if it comes to that we will be the best prepared of them all.

setting.name: Ant hill
setting.description: The ant hill is very large, over 5 feet high, and is wrapped around the base of a pine tree. The ants are huge compared to normal ants, and jut in and out of large holes in the ant hill. Bones of animals and even people can be seen sticking out of the red dirt ant hill.
setting.background: These ants are the scourge of the kingdom. Every time an ant hill is eradicated another pops up. These ants are very aggressive and hungry and have even been known to take large cattle or baby elephants.

speech: I didn't know someone else was here. Usually people don't brave the giant ants.
Well I'm quite used to it by now. Who are youZ?
Do you not recognize me?  I am just someone trying to figure out life...
Ohh I think so... are you the next heir to this kingdom?
Yes, I was hoping you wouldn't know. It would be just my luck to have anonymity for once.  I come here often to think since most people avoid it.  What brings you here?
I will not bother you like the others, don't worry. I just come here for the solitude.
Are you alone?  Have you no family or vocation?
Alone here? Yes but not alone alone, I have family in the nearest village.
I understand your need for solitude.  There are so many things that I don't agree with my father, the king, about and I'm torn between when I have to do and what I want to do.
Well if you are not happy being the heir, can you not drop the title?
I wouldn't want to disgrace my family.  I am the only child.  I know I am strong but I might do things differently one day.  Watch out...and ant is on your back!
Thank you for the watchful eye! But if you aren't happy with that path then you don't need to take it.
If only life is so easy.
I don't see the issue, but then again I am not familiar with that sort of life.
